topology_summary: The locked netlist implements an Anti-SAT-style masking structure built from two structurally near-mirror-image branches instantiated as antisat_g_inst and antisat_gbar_inst. Both branches consume the same subset of primary inputs X, but antisat_g_inst is driven by the lower key bits key[0..4] (block g(X,K_lower)) while antisat_gbar_inst is driven by the upper key bits key[5..9] (block g'(X,K_upper)) using inverted key literals relative to the matching fan-in of the first branch. The outputs of these two branches feed the gate instance antisat_gate, which combines them (AND/XOR-based gating) to produce an internal signal, antisat_out, that acts as a rarely-asserted discriminator. This antisat_out signal is then ANDed/XORed with the true functional result net, func_out_masked, so that only when the key is fully correct does func_out_masked pass through unmodified to the primary output port, out. Two of the key literals feeding antisat_gbar_inst, key[4] and key[9], are hard-tied through dedicated tie-off cells named tied_key_const_0 and tied_key_const_1 respectively, making those two bits directly and unambiguously recoverable by inspection of the netlist alone, while all remaining key bits influence only the functional correctness of func_out_masked and cannot be determined without a working oracle.
